papers.title: Capacity-controlled EEG denoising: diminishing reconstruction returns on semi-synthetic benchmarks and task-dependent downstream utility.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) denoising is often ranked by clean-reference reconstruction metrics, although downstream task performance is less often assessed. We tested capacity effects and when reconstruction fidelity tracks utility.Approach. A depthwise-separable convolutional denoiser spanned 1.05K-40.26K parameters. Capacity was evaluated on semi-synthetic clean-reference benchmarks (EEGDenoiseNet and a mixed-artifact corpus) and by zero-shot reconstruction on brain-computer interface (BCI) Competition IV-2a/IV-2b. Downstream effects and same-condition metric-utility associations used IV-2a motor imagery, with subjects as inferential units (n=9). Further tests used an IV-2b cross-session replication and within-subject paired-recording sleep staging in 75 Sleep-EDF subjects.Main results. In these semi-synthetic reconstruction settings, capacity effects depended on metric and dataset. Electrooculographic (EOG) reconstruction improved from base8 to base16 (correlation-coefficient increment 0.007264, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.005525-0.009002), whereas electromyographic (EMG) correlation coefficient met the selected practical-saturation criterion from base6 to base8. These intervals are conditional on fixed benchmark source pools; a source-level bootstrap left both classifications unchanged. On IV-2a, matched denoising reduced common spatial patterns with linear discriminant analysis (CSP+LDA) accuracy for EOG (Δ=-0.057, 95% CI -0.087 to -0.029), EMG (-0.102, -0.152 to -0.056), and mixed contamination (-0.099, -0.152 to -0.046); these effects were supported under Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (BH-FDR) control, not Holm familywise control. ShallowFBCSPNet and EEGConformer showed reductions in several conditions, whereas EEGNet and Deep4Net had no multiplicity-corrected effects. Reconstruction metrics were associated with downstream change in some EMG/mixed conditions but not consistently for EOG. In Sleep-EDF paired-recording validation, denoisers reduced sleep-stage balanced accuracy under synthetic-EOG and unmodified-recording controls; base16 changes were -0.050 and -0.074. IV-2b effects were near-null under the evaluated 01T/02T-to-03T cross-session protocol.Significance. Reconstruction fidelity is informative but not a universal surrogate endpoint. Capacity claims from semi-synthetic benchmarks should distinguish formal practical saturation from diminishing returns, and denoising evaluation should report subject-level effects and transfer controls.

ai.reason: Directly evaluates EEG denoising capacity vs downstream utility including sleep staging, offering artifact-removal insight and reproducible lightweight models relevant to the researcher's core methods.
ai.summary: A capacity-controlled EEG denoising study evaluated a depthwise-separable convolutional denoiser (1.05K–40.26K parameters) on semi-synthetic benchmarks and downstream tasks, finding that reconstruction fidelity improvements with capacity depend on metric and dataset, and that denoising often reduced downstream classification accuracy (e.g., CSP+LDA accuracy decreased for EOG, EMG, and mixed contamination on IV-2a).

papers.title: Preprocessing and feature extraction co-optimization for low-power EEG-based neurodegenerative disease detection: a benchmark on STM32 embedded platforms.
papers.abstract: Early differential diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) using electroencephalography (EEG) enables low-cost and non-invasive neurological monitoring. This study presents a lightweight TinyML framework for embedded EEG classification on resource-constrained microcontrollers. Twelve preprocessing techniques and six machine learning classifiers were evaluated on two public OpenNeuro datasets containing 88 participants. All pipelines were implemented on STM32 NUCLEO-64 and STM32WB55 platforms using INT8 quantization with CMSIS-NN. Results show that Sparse Decomposition combined with XGBoost achieved the best performance, reaching 94.46% accuracy and 92.1% sensitivity while requiring only 45 KB SRAM and low execution time, demonstrating the feasibility of wearable EEG diagnostic systems.

ai.reason: Co-optimizes preprocessing and features for low-power STM32 microcontrollers—highly transferable CPU-friendly, lightweight methodology for resource-constrained EEG analysis.
ai.summary: A lightweight TinyML framework for embedded EEG classification on STM32 microcontrollers was benchmarked using 12 preprocessing techniques and 6 classifiers on two OpenNeuro datasets (88 participants), with Sparse Decomposition combined with XGBoost achieving the best performance (94.46% accuracy, 92.1% sensitivity) while requiring only 45 KB SRAM.

papers.title: Feature processing for single-trial semantic decoding from EEG: a factorial comparison with pre-registered replication
papers.abstract: Single-trial decoding of semantic processing from EEG is used in cognitive neuroscience, brain-computer interfaces and EEG-to-text research. Because single trials are noisy, the choice of features can determine how much information a decoder uses. Yet these fields use different features that have not been compared systematically: event-related potential studies decode the voltage time course (the waveform), EEG-to-text studies mostly the power of oscillations in frequency bands. We crossed four feature-processing choices--signal representation (waveform or band power), time window, normalization and channel set--into 640 configurations and decoded whether a stimulus fitted its semantic context in three tasks: visual word pairs, objects in visual scenes, and words in spoken sentences (40 participants per task). Eleven pre-specified comparisons were tested jointly. The signal representation had by far the largest effect on accuracy (mean generalized eta squared = 0.165, an order of magnitude above any other effect). Averaged over tasks and other choices, balanced accuracy was 56.6% with the waveform and 50.6% with theta-band power (chance, 50%), and adding band power to the waveform lowered accuracy by 1.8 percentage points, in every task. Both effects replicated, and were larger, in a pre-registered study of 283 new participants from three sites. Neither a finer time-frequency decomposition including the delta band (2-4 Hz) nor a different way of combining power with the waveform changed this conclusion, whereas the time window, normalization and channel set mattered little. For semantic decoding from single EEG trials, the waveform carries the information, and band power does not add to it.

ai.reason: Systematic factorial comparison of signal representation, normalization, and channel choices directly informs reproducible, transferable EEG decoding pipelines.
ai.summary: A factorial comparison of 640 feature-processing configurations for single-trial EEG semantic decoding across three tasks showed that signal representation had the largest effect: waveform features achieved 56.6% balanced accuracy versus 50.6% for theta-band power, and adding band power to waveform reduced accuracy by 1.8 percentage points; these effects replicated and were larger in a pre-registered study of 283 new participants.

papers.title: A post-training quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification.
papers.abstract: Sleep classification models play a crucial role in assessing sleep quality. Although the classification performance of these models has continuously improved in recent years, significant accuracy degradation is commonly observed when quantizing and deploying them on edge devices with limited memory and computational resources. To address this challenge, we propose a posttraining quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification. Specifically, we first identify convolutional and linear layers within the model, then compute layerwise sensitivities based on each layer's input. We dynamically adjust the threshold for each layer based on its sensitivity, using this threshold to detect abnormal weights causing excessive quantization error in that layer. To ensure quantization accuracy, we preserve these abnormal weights at their original precision while compressing the remaining weights to 4 bits. After quantizing each layer, we employ dynamic low-rank compensation to correct quantization errors and further enhance accuracy, addressing information loss during quantization. Experiments on the Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78 and SHHS datasets demonstrate that our method achieves near-lossless compression: the accuracy of the vast majority of sleep classification models drops by less than 1%, while reducing model size by nearly 8 times. This work provides the first general framework for post-training quantization of sleep classification models, offering a new approach for the practical deployment of these models on edge devices.

ai.reason: Directly targets CPU/edge-friendly sleep-stage classification with quantization and reproducible accuracy preservation—highly relevant to lightweight sleep staging.
ai.summary: A post-training quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification was proposed, using layer-wise sensitivity-based thresholds and dynamic low-rank compensation to compress models to 4 bits, achieving near-lossless accuracy (drop <1%) while reducing model size by nearly 8x across Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS datasets.

papers.title: Sleep as a window into thalamocortical pathology: generative modeling implicates NMDA receptor hypofunction in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
papers.abstract: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a strong genetic risk factor for neuropsychiatric conditions, including schizophrenia, yet the underlying synaptic mechanisms remain unclear. Sleep EEG suggests thalamocortical dysfunction, but scalp data alone lack mechanistic resolution. Computational modelling can bridge this gap by inferring receptor-level dynamics from EEG. We applied a conductance-based thalamocortical Dynamic Causal Model (DCM) to sleep-wake EEG from children with 22q11.2DS (n=28) and their neurotypical siblings (n=17), estimating contributions of AMPA, NMDA, GABAA, and GABAB conductances. Building on these estimates, we investigated which receptor systems, if perturbed, could shift circuit dynamics toward sibling patterns. To address this, we implemented in silico pharmacology by systematically scaling receptor-mediated conductances. Increasing NMDA receptor (NMDA-R) efficacy consistently produced the strongest improvements in alignment with sibling spectra (effect size = 0.32 in light NREM, 0.45 in deep NREM), whereas AMPA- or GABA-based manipulations were weaker. The most influential pathways were recurrent NMDA-R excitation among superficial pyramidal cells and NMDA-R excitation from spiny stellates to superficial pyramidal populations. Exploratory regressions linked greater thalamocortical delay during deep sleep to greater sleep problems (β=0.34, pFDR=0.006), and AMPA-mediated excitation of interneurons during wakefulness to anxiety symptoms (β=-0.32, pFDR=0.032). These findings implicate NMDA receptor hypofunction as a key mechanism in 22q11.2DS and suggest it may serve as a treatment target. We further show that DCM-based virtual pharmacology can simulate drug-level interventions, and we are now testing whether NMDA receptor modulation restores network activity in preclinical models (e.g., mouse models of 22q11.2DS).
authors: Marianne B M van den Bree

papers.title: Integrating convolutional variational autoencoders and the Gaussian mixture model for efficient manifold learning and clustering of spatially preserved EEG topographic maps.
papers.abstract: EEG microstate analysis segments continuous brain activity into brief, quasi-stable topographic configurations whose quantity, duration, and transition dynamics index cognitive state and neuropsychiatric conditions. The standard algorithm, modified k-means (ModKMeans), operates in electrode space. It performs hard partitioning, assigning each data point to exactly one cluster, and provides no learned representation, no generative decoder, and no probabilistic soft assignment. In this research, a Convolutional Variational Deep Embedding model (Conv-VaDE) is designed, a topographic-map adaptation of Variational Deep Embedding (VaDE) that places a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) prior on the latent space of a convolutional variational autoencoder and jointly trains the encoder, decoder, and GMM. Microstate polarity invariance, the property that a topography [Formula: see text] and its sign-inverted counterpart [Formula: see text] index the same underlying configuration, is preserved through three coordinated mechanisms: sign-flip augmentation of the training set, a polarity-invariant reconstruction loss, and an encoder regulariser on the latent embedding. The model is evaluated on a sample of healthy participants ([Formula: see text] healthy adults, eyes-closed) from the LEMON resting-state EEG dataset using a multi-quadrant evaluation framework, with each method assessed in its native frame and cross-method comparisons performed via rank-based Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Conv-VaDE instead offers a focused set of capabilities the standard ModKMeans pipeline does not provide: a learned generative latent manifold (silhouette 0.232 at [Formula: see text], with very narrow cross-subject interquartile-range width [Formula: see text] across the 203 participants, indicating highly reproducible latent geometry), decoded GMM cluster centres inspectable as scalp topographies, probabilistic soft assignment for transitional states, and a generative framework supporting downstream representation analysis. A rank-based meta-criterion over silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz, and Davies-Bouldin yields modal [Formula: see text] for Conv-VaDE (39.4%) and [Formula: see text] for ModKMeans (29.6%); [Formula: see text] is adopted to align with the canonical Lehmann A/B/C/D literature. Within the classical cluster-validity register, ModKMeans attains a higher silhouette and 4-5 percentage points higher Global Explained Variance at every K (Wilcoxon, BH-corrected, [Formula: see text]). The two methods occupy distinct positions in the methodological design space, with the cross-method comparison characterising the trade-off between direct electrode-space optimisation and learned generative representation rather than adjudicating method superiority.

papers.title: Before synchrony: the unresolved specificity of neural oscillations across brains.
papers.abstract: EEG hyperscanning studies frequently report inter-brain synchrony across a wide range of frequencies, topographies, and social tasks. However, the interpretation of these findings usually relies on canonical frequency bands and builds on the assumption that oscillations are stable, sustained, and comparable across individuals. Yet, single-brain electrophysiology increasingly shows that neural oscillations are shaped by 1/f aperiodic activity, with important inter- and intra-individual differences in their properties, and with some frequency bands manifesting as short transient bursts rather than sustained rhythms. These properties are rarely addressed in hyperscanning research. They also interact with standard analytical pipelines, which implicitly assume sustained oscillations at a shared frequency across partners. Drawing on recent advances in neural oscillation research, the paper argues that IBS research should move beyond descriptive reports of synchrony and instead formulate mechanistically grounded hypotheses specifying why synchrony is expected in particular frequencies and brain regions, to build interpretable accounts of inter-brain dynamics.

ai.topic: Aperiodic activity and transient bursts critique of hyperscanning
ai.reason: Directly addresses 1/f aperiodic activity, transient oscillation bursts, and normalization assumptions that affect spectral analysis pipelines, providing strongly relevant methodological cautions for time-frequency work.
ai.summary: A commentary arguing that EEG hyperscanning research should move beyond descriptive inter-brain synchrony reports by accounting for 1/f aperiodic activity and transient oscillatory bursts, and should formulate mechanistically grounded hypotheses specifying why synchrony is expected in particular frequencies and regions.

papers.title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation increases slow waves during human NREM sleep
papers.abstract: Slow waves are a hallmark of sleep homeostasis and a target for enhancing restorative sleep. Transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) can non-invasively deliver a low-frequency envelope to deep targets and has been shown to increase spectral slow-wave activity during sleep. It remains untested whether tTIS also alters discrete slow waves, how their cortical expression changes, and whether the field each brain receives relates to the response. During non-rapid eye movement sleep, 32 participants received 1 Hz tTIS and 11 a carrier-only control in 3-min episodes targeting the left insula/ventromedial prefrontal cortex. Combining high-density electroencephalography (EEG), source reconstruction and individualized field modeling, we found that tTIS increased slow-wave density by about 20% during and 30% after stimulation, across shallow and deep waves, with limited morphology change. The carrier-only control showed no detected density change. In source space, each wave involved more cortex in both arms, while wave origins did not change. A dose-response analysis showed that tTIS participants who received a stronger modeled field shifted further toward N3 sleep during stimulation, a relation not seen in the control. These results support tTIS as a candidate EEG-compatible tool for modulating slow waves and motivate individualized field modeling to interpret its effects.

papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, Electroencephalography, and Electromyography with Intracortical Electrical Stimulation in Freely Moving Mice.
papers.abstract: Simultaneously combining cellular-resolution imaging, electrical neuromodulation, and electrophysiological monitoring in freely moving mice requires a mechanically stable chronic implant and precise synchronization across recording systems. This protocol describes an integrated preparation for cortical two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, electroencephalography (EEG), and electromyography (EMG) in freely moving, tethered mice. Using the retrosplenial cortex as an example target, the protocol details fabrication and implantation of the cranial window and electrodes, viral delivery, optical field localization, installation of a detachable imaging interface, behavioral habituation, multimodal data acquisition, and stimulation-aligned calcium-signal analysis. The preparation permits repeated optical access over short- and long-term intervals and generates cellular-resolution calcium signals together with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measurements. Representative outputs include continuous multimodal session-level recordings, mouse-level population calcium responses, and paired stimulation-off and stimulation-on response measures. The workflow can be adapted to other experimentally accessible cortical targets by modifying the cranial-window location, viral injection coordinates, electrode trajectory, and implant geometry.

ai.reason: Chronic multimodal mouse EEG/EMG/calcium protocol relevant to animal sleep experiments, though more a surgical/recording protocol than a computational method.
ai.summary: Describes a protocol integrating two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, EEG, and EMG in freely moving tethered mice using a stable chronic cranial-window/electrode implant, with the retrosplenial cortex as target. The preparation yields cellular-resolution calcium signals with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measures and supports stimulation-aligned response analysis.

papers.title: Noise resilience in brain decoding driven by spiking neural networks for responsive robot control.
papers.abstract: Brain computer interface (BCI) is a promising technology, expanding on many fields ranging from medical to commercial applications. The diffusion of this technique is compromised by the complexity of the treated data and the unavoidable presence of noise in those systems. This study contributes to the solution of this problem by proposing a BCI pipeline that relies on the use of spiking neural networks (SNNs), quantifying their robustness to noise in the context of brain decoding through the classification of Electroencephalography (EEG). We benchmark a shallow convolutional network against two spiking counterparts based on leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) and adaptive LIF neurons on the four-class BNCI 2014-001 motor imagery dataset. The conventional model has a slight advantage in clean conditions, but it degrades dramatically once the input is corrupted. In contrast, SNN demonstrates remarkable robustness under signal degradation. Under global Gaussian noise, CNN accuracy drops by 58.56%, whereas Adaptive LIF SNN accuracy drops by only 0.80%. Similarly, when trained on recordings with one electrode removed and tested on the complete montage, CNN loses 36.00% of its accuracy, compared with 0.34% for the SNN. With semi-simulated ocular, muscular and cardiac artifacts the gap is smaller, but the spiking models still degrade less than the CNN for every artifact type. This robustness is obtained at equal model size with 18.0 of the 24.6 MMAC required per trial by the baseline replaced by accumulate-only, spike-driven operations. Finally, the spiking model was integrated in a full decoding-to-actuation pipeline driving a Franka Emika Research 3 robot from a replayed EEG stream. These findings indicate that, compared with a dense counterpart, spiking computation substantially reduces the sensitivity of EEG decoding to signal corruption, which supports the use of SNNs in deployments where robustness matters more than peak accuracy.

ai.reason: Introduces noise-resilience and electrode-dropout robustness in EEG classification, a transferable methodological idea relevant to artifact/robustness concerns, though spiking network focus and robot BCI application limit direct utility.
ai.summary: Benchmarked shallow CNN and LIF/adaptive-LIF spiking neural networks for four-class EEG motor imagery decoding on the BNCI 2014-001 dataset and integrated the spiking model into a decoding-to-robot-control pipeline. Spiking models were far more noise-robust than the CNN: under global Gaussian noise CNN accuracy dropped 58.56% versus 0.80% for adaptive LIF, and with one electrode removed CNN lost 36.00% versus 0.34%.

papers.title: EEG Decoding in Context: A Framework for Tuning-Free EEG Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoding is a central route toward brain-computer interfaces for communication, rehabilitation, cognitive assessment, and neurological monitoring. Recent EEG foundation models have substantially advanced reusable signal representations, but their downstream use still typically requires a task-specific decoder, gradient-based adaptation, and validation-driven model selection. We investigate a complementary foundation-model paradigm based on in-context learning: labeled EEG recordings define the decoding task as context, and new recordings are predicted without updating model parameters. We first pair raw EEG features with a pretrained general-purpose in-context predictor. This direct formulation provides a promising starting point, but its performance remains limited and unstable and does not generalize reliably across EEG paradigms. We find that suitable context construction can address these limitations by improving the effective signal-to-noise ratio and exposing temporal and spatial structure. Building on this insight, we introduce a general framework that combines EEG-specific context construction with a frozen in-context predictor and a metric-based context adaptation mechanism, which matches each downstream task to an appropriate context representation without relying on validation data. Across ten datasets spanning seven EEG decoding paradigms, our method achieves the highest mean BAcc among eleven specialized and fine-tuned EEG baselines, without task-specific parameter updates or validation-based model selection. This framework provides a practical path toward tuning-free EEG foundation models in which adaptation is expressed through context rather than parameter updates.

ai.reason: Explores calibration-free decoding without gradient updates, relevant to user calibration from small labeled data and adaptable across paradigms, though foundation-model oriented.
ai.summary: Introduces a tuning-free EEG foundation-model framework using in-context learning with EEG-specific context construction, a frozen in-context predictor, and metric-based context adaptation, requiring no parameter updates or validation-driven model selection. Across ten datasets spanning seven EEG decoding paradigms it achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy among eleven specialized and fine-tuned baselines.

papers.title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have long sought calibration-free operation, yet classifiers are typically benchmarked on discrimination alone. Discrimination is blind to calibration, a meaningful gap given that electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are nonstationary and point-estimate classifiers can become overconfident under distribution shift. We conducted a large-scale study contrasting Bayesian complete-pooling models against frequentist baselines for cross-subject, left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery EEG classification across 20 datasets. Each of six frequentist pipelines was paired with an analogous Bayesian pipeline sharing identical, deterministic feature extraction, so that only the classifier was Bayesian. Bayesian classifiers were fit via Markov chain Monte Carlo posterior sampling. Our primary metric was the Brier score, decomposed into reliability and resolution, alongside the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for discrimination and Shannon entropy for sharpness. For each metric we fit a random-effects meta-analysis with Knapp-Hartung adjustment, verified by leave-one-out influence analysis. Bayesian complete-pooling produced statistically significant improvements in reliability and increases in predictive uncertainty (lower sharpness), with 95% confidence intervals of [-0.0029, -0.0001] for reliability and [0.0022, 0.0220] bits for entropy. Still, neither effect held statistical significance when datasets with flagged posterior sampling were excluded. Brier score, resolution, and discrimination showed no significant differences. Between-study heterogeneity was low across all metrics. Bayesian pipelines consumed roughly thirteen times more energy than their frequentist counterparts, a cost that remains modest relative to common household appliances. This modest cost makes partial-pooling across subjects and sessions, the structure complete-pooling omits, a feasible next step.

ai.reason: Addresses calibration-free cross-subject classification and calibration/confidence via Bayesian pooling—relevant to user calibration with small labeled data, though motor-imagery focused.
ai.summary: Compared Bayesian complete-pooling classifiers against matched frequentist pipelines for cross-subject left- versus right-hand motor imagery EEG across 20 datasets, using Brier score decomposition, AUC, and entropy with random-effects meta-analysis. Bayesian models significantly improved reliability and increased predictive uncertainty, but these effects disappeared when flagged posterior-sampling datasets were excluded, and Bayesian pipelines consumed roughly 13 times more energy.

papers.title: Condition-associated EEG signatures in N-back tasks: temporal dynamics, classification, and generalization.
papers.abstract: Mental workload (MWL) monitoring with electroencephalography (EEG) is promising for adaptive systems, but practical use requires models that remain reliable across time, tasks, and users with feasible sensor layouts. This study investigated condition-associated EEG signatures in 15 healthy adults performing two complementary N-back paradigms: an N-back level manipulation (N-LEVELS: 1-back, 2-back, 3-back) and a stimulus-pacing manipulation at fixed 2-back (N-SPEED: slow, medium, fast). EEG was recorded using a compact 8-channel setup. Spectral bandpower features, composite workload indices, and N2/P3b ERP markers were analyzed. Linear classifiers were evaluated using within-subject TRAIN → TEST and leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocols, together with analyses of observation duration, time-on-task dynamics, temporal generalization, cross-paradigm transfer, and exploratory ordinal regression. N-LEVELS and N-SPEED produced distinct behavioral and subjective profiles: increasing N-back level was associated with greater task demand, whereas faster N-SPEED conditions showed greater perceived temporal demand and reduced response-time availability. Exploratory locally corrected spectral analyses suggested more frequent beta-band and engagement-index modulation in N-LEVELS and more frequent posterior/parietal alpha suppression and theta/alpha-related modulation in N-SPEED. ERP analyses showed reduced P3b amplitude under higher N-back levels and faster pacing. Classification performance was modest and context-dependent: N-SPEED three-class decoding was more consistent than N-LEVELS, and all three N-SPEED pairwise contrasts survived correction under both WITHIN and LOSO evaluation, whereas in N-LEVELS only the 1-back vs. 3-back contrast survived under LOSO. Post hoc artifact-sensitivity analyses supported the principal P3b findings and largely preserved reference-decoding and alpha time-on-task patterns. After delta-band removal, neither three-class LOSO result nor the N-SPEED slow-vs.-medium and medium-vs.-fast LOSO contrasts survived correction; N-SPEED slow vs. medium under LOSO also did not survive either high-pass variant. Exploratory ordinal regression showed a clearer ordered relationship for N-SPEED than N-LEVELS. Time-on-task analyses revealed selective non-stationarity, mainly progressive alpha build-up, whereas cross-paradigm transfer did not survive corrected inference. These findings indicate that compact EEG recordings contain condition-associated information, but the small sample, deterministic block order, modest decoding performance, and limited cross-paradigm generalization constrain causal attribution and applicability beyond the present protocol.

ai.reason: Compact 8-channel setup with temporal/cross-paradigm generalization and LOSO analyses relevant to transferable vigilance-state classification, though workload-focused.
ai.summary: Examined condition-associated EEG signatures in 15 healthy adults performing N-back level (1/2/3-back) and stimulus-pacing manipulations with an 8-channel setup, analyzing bandpower, workload indices, N2/P3b ERPs, and classifier generalization. P3b amplitude decreased with higher load and faster pacing; N-SPEED three-class decoding generalized more consistently than N-LEVELS, but cross-paradigm transfer did not survive correction and decoding was constrained by small sample and deterministic block order.

papers.title: CFCR-Net: cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection.
papers.abstract: rConventional electroencephalography (EEG) frequency-domain analysis relies on predefined spectral bands and treats them as independent features, neglecting spectral variability and dynamic cross-band interactions. We propose a cross-frequency synergy representation paradigm and the Cross-Frequency Connectivity Reorganization Network (CFCR-Net), coupling wavelet packet sub-band decomposition with adaptive cross-frequency graph learning: orthogonalized amplitude correlation constructs a sub-band connectivity graph, and graph convolution propagates cross-frequency information. On SEED-VIG, CFCR-Net achieves 0.8831 accuracy, 0.9102 F1-score, and 75.2% leave-one-subject-out cross-subject accuracy. Visualization reveals coupling reorganizing from middle- and high-frequency toward low-frequency-dominated connectivity as fatigue develops, providing interpretable evidence of fatigue-state evolution.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering

ai.reason: Spectral/time-frequency sub-band connectivity and interpretable state-detection method transferable to vigilance classification, though driver-fatigue specific.
ai.summary: Proposes CFCR-Net, a cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning framework that couples wavelet packet sub-band decomposition with adaptive cross-frequency graph learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection. On SEED-VIG it achieved 0.8831 accuracy, 0.9102 F1-score, and 75.2% cross-subject accuracy, with visualization showing fatigue-related connectivity reorganizing toward low-frequency dominance.

papers.title: A Neuro-Inspired Dual-Pathway Attention Network for EEG-Based Identity Recognition.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals have shown promise for biometric recognition due to their intrinsic liveness detection. However, their practical deployment remains limited. The main obstacles are non-stationary drift, scarce labeled data, and fluctuating signal quality. Most existing models adopt static computation graphs, which are ill-equipped to handle these variations. We propose a dual-pathway architecture that separates a data-driven bottom-up perceptual extractor from a prior-guided top-down modulator. A quality-aware gate computes instantaneous signal stability from channel-wise and temporal variances. It dynamically fuses the two pathways: bottom-up features dominate when the signal is clean, and identity priors take over when noise is high. Deep residual connections and pyramid fusion stabilize multi-scale learning. On the DEAP dataset, our method achieves 93.8% accuracy, which is 5.3 percentage points higher than the best baseline. On THU-EP, it reaches 97.2%. In cross-session tests on the noisy SEED-IV dataset, performance drops only 2.5% in Session 2 and 5.2% in Session 3. With only 1% of the training data on THU-EP, the model still attains 76.8% accuracy. Dynamic, signal-dependent fusion improves accuracy, cross-session robustness, and data efficiency. This work offers a practical, low-enrollment solution for patient identity verification, electronic health record access, and brain-computer interface authentication in clinical and mobile settings. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/cangtianhaoxue/ DPRAN.git.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

ai.summary: The authors propose a dual-pathway attention network for EEG-based identity recognition that separates bottom-up perceptual feature extraction from top-down prior-guided modulation, fused by a quality-aware gate based on instantaneous signal stability. The method achieved 93.8% accuracy on DEAP (5.3 percentage points above the best baseline) and 97.2% on THU-EP, with only 2.5% and 5.2% performance drops in cross-session tests on noisy SEED-IV and 76.8% accuracy with only 1% of training data on THU-EP.

papers.title: PRISM-MP: Psychology-guided and reliability-aware multimodal learning for cross-musician emotion recognition during musical performance.
papers.abstract: Emotion classification during active musical performance is challenging because neural activity, cardiac dynamics, and acoustic expression provide complementary but non-equivalent evidence of intended emotional communication and self-reported affect. This study presents PRISM-MP, a psychology-guided and reliability-aware multimodal framework for cross-musician emotion recognition. We analyzed a publicly available dataset comprising synchronized electroencephalography, electrocardiography, and musical audio recordings from 11 experienced musicians who performed excerpts intended to communicate happiness, sadness, anger, or relaxation. PRISM-MP integrates dynamic frequency-specific electroencephalographic functional graphs with affine-invariant tangent-space covariance representations, models multiscale physiological dynamics, and applies class-conditional source-domain alignment to reduce musician-specific distributional differences. The physiological and acoustic pathways receive auxiliary supervision from felt and communicated valence-arousal ratings, respectively. Their contributions are dynamically adjusted according to signal quality, predictive uncertainty, and cross-modal disagreement. Under nested source-only leave-one-musician-out evaluation, PRISM-MP achieved a musician-macro-averaged performance-level accuracy of 92.14%, balanced accuracy of 91.82%, macro-F1 of 0.910, Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.892, and expected calibration error of 0.041. Against the strongest recent source-only EEG baseline evaluated under the same protocol, the corresponding gains were 3.91 percentage points in balanced accuracy and 0.037 in macro-F1. The framework remained robust when electrocardiography or audio was unavailable and under partial electroencephalographic channel loss. A systematic leave-one-channel-out analysis across 29 EEG electrodes revealed nonuniform channel sensitivity. Removing C3, Cz, C4, and F3 produced the largest balanced-accuracy reductions of 2.22, 2.05, 2.02, and 1.90 percentage points, respectively, while removal of several other channels produced minimal changes. Computational profiling indicated 3.46 million trainable parameters and processing times of 74 ms with GPU-supported audio embedding and 312 ms on a desktop CPU, while physiological encoding and fusion required 18.7 ms after feature preparation. These timings exclude the 30-s observation period and do not represent end-to-end interactive latency. A secondary post hoc within-recording calibration analysis increased macro-F1 to 0.946 using a lightweight residual adapter. These findings support reliability-aware physiological-acoustic modeling as a computational foundation for future musician-centered affective interfaces.

papers.title: Hypothalamic orexin input to the medial amygdala promotes arousal from anaesthesia and modulates exploratory behaviour.
papers.abstract: Emergence from general anaesthesia is often accompanied by agitation, suggesting that recovery of consciousness can engage neural circuits that regulate arousal and behavioural responsiveness. The amygdala influences social, defensive, and exploratory behaviours, but whether orexinergic input to the amygdala regulates anaesthetic state transitions together with behavioural responses remains unclear. In male orexin-Cre mice, we combined viral tracing, electrophysiology, and RNAscope to define a lateral hypothalamic orexin (LHAOx) projection to the medial amygdala (MeA). Optogenetics, electroencephalography, electromyography, and fibre photometry were used to test how this circuit regulates arousal from isoflurane anaesthesia, as well as exploratory and place-preference behaviour. LHAOx neurones densely innervated the MeA, where orexin receptor 2 was more abundant than orexin receptor 1 (P<0.0001). Optogenetic activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection promoted arousal from 0.75 vol% isoflurane sedation (P<0.0001), delayed induction by 3 vol% isoflurane as measured by loss of the righting reflex (P=0.0074), and accelerated emergence from 2 vol% isoflurane as measured by return of the righting reflex (P=0.0098). In behavioural assays, activation of this projection suppressed open-field exploration, increased real-time place preference, and did not produce conditioned place preference. Activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection was accompanied by increased activity in MeA vesicular GABA transporter (MeAvGAT)-expressing neurones. Direct activation of MeAvGAT neurones replicated the arousal-promoting and reduced exploratory behaviour, whereas silencing their synaptic output eliminated the induction-delaying effect and shifted the real-time preference. The LHAOx projection to the MeA promotes anaesthetic arousal and acutely suppresses exploratory behaviour in male mice, with MeAvGAT serving as a key downstream target.

Medial amygdala vesicular GABA transporter (MeAvGAT) neurons acted as a key downstream target, replicating arousal-promoting and reduced exploratory effects.

papers.title: Time-dependent alterations of the heart-brain axis in rats following a single microwave exposure.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the time-dependent changes and possible mechanisms of the heart-brain axis in rats following S-band microwave exposure. A single microwave exposure model was established using 8-week-old male Wistar rats (2.856 GHz, 50 mW/cm², 30 min). At Days 1, 3, and 7 post-exposure, we evaluated electrocardiogram, heart rate variability, and electroencephalogram activities, alongside serum biochemical and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay indicators. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of the hippocampus and myocardium, combined with real-time quantitative PCR, were utilized to validate key molecular changes. The results showed that following a single exposure, the function of the rat heart-brain axis changed in a time-dependent but outcome-specific manner: neuroendocrine, autonomic, and electroencephalographic alterations were most evident on Day 1, most circulating cardiac and brain injury markers were highest on Day 3, and lactate dehydrogenase increased only on Day 7. These changes were primarily characterized by imbalanced autonomic nervous function and heart rate variability, abnormal electrocardiogram and electroencephalogram activities, and elevated injury-related markers. Integrated multi-omics analysis revealed significant molecular remodeling in both tissues on Day 3. Myocardial differential molecules were primarily enriched in cytochrome P450-mediated metabolism and detoxification pathways, with representative molecules including Adh6 and Cyp4f5. Hippocampal differential molecules mainly involved neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions, neural signal transduction, and synaptic regulation pathways, with representative molecules including Adra2b and Chrna3. These findings suggest that a S-band microwave exposure induces heart-brain axis autonomic regulatory imbalance, electrophysiological abnormalities, and synchronized changes in central neural signaling and peripheral metabolic detoxification. These results provide an experimental basis for risk assessment and protective strategies against high-power microwaves.

papers.title: Propofol rapidly reverses cognitive impairments with restoration of sleep stability and alleviation of neuroinflammation in sleep-deprived mice.
papers.abstract: Acute total sleep deprivation (SD) produces immediate and severe cognitive impairments. Although propofol has been shown to be effective against cognitive impairments under certain SD circumstances, its pharmacological profile under acute total SD remains to be further explored. The present study found that a single subanesthetic bolus of propofol (35-50 mg/kg, i.p.) rapidly ameliorated acute total SD-induced cognitive impairments, with effects observed as early as one hour after administration and persisting for 24 hours in the Y-maze test, whereas the classical hypnotic zolpidem (ZPD, 1.25-5 mg/kg) was ineffective in rescuing cognition. Propofol's cognitive-improving effect was also demonstrated in novel object recognition and object location recognition tasks. Meanwhile, non-invasive sleep monitoring revealed that propofol increased the proportions of medium-to-long duration non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep (64-128 seconds), and reduced the episode numbers of short-duration NREM sleep (0-4, 4-8, and 8-16 seconds) in SD mice. EEG/EMG recordings confirmed that propofol increased total NREM duration by prolonging mean episode duration. In contrast, ZPD failed to reverse NREM sleep fragmentation under either monitoring modality, although it did prolong total NREM sleep duration. Moreover, propofol upregulated the core circadian regulator BMAL1, reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and TNF-α), restored the expression of key neuroplasticity-related proteins (BDNF, PSD-95, and SYN), and reversed SD-induced loss of dendritic spines in the hippocampus. Together, these findings suggest that propofol rapidly ameliorates SD-induced cognitive impairments, and that this behavioral rescue is associated with the restoration of sleep stability and attenuation of neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled quality assurance for point-of-care electroencephalographic cap placement by inexperienced users.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) remains inaccessible in many health care settings, including low- and middle-income countries and point-of-care environments where trained EEG technologists are unavailable. Although low-cost EEG systems enable inexperienced users to acquire EEG, reliable acquisition also requires quality assurance of accurate electrode array positioning. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tool to address this need. We conducted a prospective randomized crossover validation study comparing AI-guided EEG cap fitting by inexperienced users with placement by an expert EEG technologist. A blinded expert quantified positioning error against International 10-20 System targets and independently rated overall placement as optimal, usable, or incorrect. Thirty participants completed 60 placement trials. Mean absolute positioning error was .938 cm with app-guided and .855 cm with expert placement. The mean paired difference was .084 cm (90% confidence interval = .024-.143), demonstrating noninferiority against the prespecified .5-cm margin. Clinically acceptable placement (optimal or usable) was achieved in 28 of 30 (93.3%) app-guided and 30 of 30 (100%) expert trials. AI-enabled quality assurance enabled inexperienced users to achieve electrode array positioning noninferior to expert placement, supporting its potential use in expanding access to point-of-care EEG.

papers.title: Performance evaluation of smart ring-derived sleep parameters compared with portable electroencephalography in university students.
papers.abstract: Wearable devices enable convenient assessment of sleep in daily life. Smart rings facilitate long-term monitoring; however, their agreement with electroencephalography (EEG)-based sleep assessment remains unclear. We evaluated the performance of the SOXAI RING -derived sleep parameters against those obtained using a portable EEG device. Of 52 university students enrolled, 49 (mean age 19.3 years; 42 females) were included in the final analysis. Participants underwent simultaneous overnight monitoring with the SOXAI RING (SOXAI Co., Ltd.) and portable EEG device (Proassist Co., Ltd.) under habitual home sleeping conditions. Total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), wake after sleep onset (WASO), and sleep stages were compared between devices. Epoch-by-epoch (EBE) analyses were also performed to evaluate sleep-wake and four-stage sleep classification. A strong correlation for TST was observed between devices (ρ = 0.70, p < 0.01). Bland-Altman analysis showed that the SOXAI RING tended to underestimate TST and light sleep, while overestimating WASO and deep sleep. In EBE analysis, the SOXAI RING showed high sensitivity for sleep but low specificity for wake. For four-stage classification, the overall accuracy was 50.0% and Cohen's κ was 0.27. The SOXAI RING showed good performance for estimating TST and may be useful for long-term sleep monitoring under habitual home conditions. However, EBE analysis demonstrated limited performance for wake detection and sleep-stage classification. Sleep-stage estimates and sleep fragmentation metrics should therefore be interpreted cautiously, and further refinement of sleep-staging algorithms is warranted.

papers.title: Generalizable mapping of the Epileptogenic Zone from interictal Intracranial EEG using an implant topology-aware Transformer
papers.abstract: Presurgical localization of the epileptogenic zone remains a central challenge in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. At the same time, the abundant interictal intracranial EEG (iEEG) data routinely acquired during presurgical evaluation remain an underexploited source of localizing information. We developed an iEEG implant topology-aware transformer that combines interictal iEEG features with electrode coordinates to predict resection targets. The model was trained exclusively on three public datasets (n = 476) and tested on cohorts from five independent centers across three countries (n = 216). In patients with favorable surgical outcomes (Engel I; n = 120), the median area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.71, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.92, outperforming interictal spike rate and clinically defined seizure-onset zone baselines in patients with favorable outcomes (P < 0.05 for both AUPRC and AUROC). Patients with unfavorable outcomes (Engel II-IV; n = 96) had lower prediction-resection alignment (median AUPRC, 0.42), and their highest confidence predictions were located farther from resected tissue (P = 0.005). These findings establish a generalizable framework that integrates neural activity and brain topology to identify epileptogenic tissue from interictal recordings, potentially improving surgical success rates and reducing reliance on resource-intensive seizure capture.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.abstract: While MEG source localization pipelines often employ head models of one single compartment with homogeneous conductivity, researchers and clinicians use at least 3 different layers in head models for EEG source localization. Recent AI-based segmentation makes it possible to generate individualized head models with 40 high-resolution, non-nested tissues. We present a pipeline that can make use of, and test, these highly realistic models for EEG source localization: with the boundary element fast multipole method (BEM-FMM), we compute transcranial electric stimulation (TES) solutions on the full 40-tissue geometry and use them reciprocally to obtain the EEG leadfields. Out approach runs on a single modest workstation, requiring approximately 4.5 min per EEG channel for a mesh of about one million elements at a relative residual of 1e-4. We applied the pipeline to six participants undergoing intermittent photic stimulation at half their individual alpha peak frequency, comparing 61-channel EEG source localizations from 40-tissue and 5-layer models with each other and with localizations from simultaneously recorded MEG. We further compared noiseless synthetic EEG topographies of the two models across the entire cortex. The two models produced highly consistent EEG source localizations (weighed relative difference below 3%), both in close agreement with the MEG localizations within the visual cortex. The synthetic topographies also agreed closely, with differences scaling approximately linearly with the angle between the source orientations of the two models, underscoring the importance of accurate source normals in fixed-orientation source models. These results establish 40-tissue models as a practical and robust basis for EEG source localization, and open the way to applications where nested geometries cannot represent the anatomy, such as infants or patients with skull defects, injuries, or tumors.

The two models produced highly consistent EEG source localizations (weighted relative difference below 3%), both in close agreement with MEG localizations within the visual cortex, establishing 40-tissue models as a practical and robust basis for EEG source localization.

papers.title: Hybrid coati-gozde optimization-based EEG channel selection for automated alcoholism detection.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlcohol addiction has significant physical, psychological, and social consequences, making early detection highly important for effective treatment. Electroencephalogram (EEG) provides a reliable means for such assessment; however, using a large number of EEG channels in real-time systems increases dimensionality and computational overhead.ObjectiveTo overcome this challenge, a novel hybridized optimization algorithm called COA-GOZDE is proposed to identify the optimal channel.MethodsThis research uses Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) to extract sub-band components from EEG signals. Statistical features are computed from Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) in the time domain and classification of addicted and non-addicted subjects is carried out using k-Nearest Neighbour, Random Forest and Multi-Layer Perceptron classifiers. For optimal channel selection, a hybrid optimization strategy is developed by integrating the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) with the Gozde Optimization Algorithm (GOZDE).ResultsThe proposed COA-GOZDE achieves an accuracy of 94.6% with only 14 EEG channels, representing a substantial reduction from the original 61 while maintaining classification performance. Comparative experiments with standard optimization algorithms such as GWO, HHO, WOA and COA confirm the superiority of the hybrid algorithm in both accuracy and efficiency.ConclusionCOA-GOZDE effectively minimizes channel count by 79.34% without compromising detection performance, establishing a strong contribution to EEG-based alcohol addiction identification.

papers.title: Preparatory beta activity reflects the precision demands of an upcoming movement
papers.abstract: Noise and external disturbances continuously push the limb away from its intended path, but not every deviation compromises the goal of an action. The accuracy constraints of a task define the range of acceptable endpoints and thereby set its precision demands, that is, how much noise must be attenuated for the task to succeed. Whether neural activity during movement preparation reflects these precision demands remains largely unexplored. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while healthy human participants (n = 27) prepared reaching movements toward narrow or wide targets at the same location and with the same timing constraints. An instructed delay before the go cue allowed preparatory activity to be isolated, and mechanical perturbations were applied during movement to probe feedback responses. Narrow targets led to more precise movements, with greater endpoint accuracy, lower variability and smaller perturbation-induced deviations. This was achieved without a reduction in movement speed, and involved greater muscle co-activation and larger long-latency responses to perturbations. Before movement onset, beta power (13-30 Hz) was lower for narrow than for wide targets, an effect that emerged late in the delay period and was concentrated over bilateral parieto-occipital electrodes. In contrast, alpha (8-12 Hz) and theta (4-7 Hz) activity did not differ between conditions. These findings demonstrate that preparatory beta activity is sensitive not only to kinematic requirements of the movement but also the precision with which it must be produced.

Narrow targets also produced more precise movements, greater muscle co-activation, and larger long-latency perturbation responses, indicating preparatory beta reflects task precision demands.

papers.title: NeuroMotion: Aligning EEG to Discrete Motion Primitives for Continuous Motion Decoding
papers.abstract: EEG-to-motion decoding remains challenging because noisy scalp EEG is difficult to map directly to continuous kinematics. We present NeuroMotion, a framework that aligns EEG representations to discrete motion primitives for continuous motion decoding across heterogeneous paradigms, including full-body free movement, lower-limb treadmill locomotion, and upper-limb freewill reaching and grasping. A VQ-based motion prior discretizes continuous motion into reusable primitives that serve as both alignment prototypes and intermediate prediction targets. Prototypical and supervised contrastive objectives align EEG embeddings to motion-derived prototypes and organize them according to primitive assignments. An E2M Transformer predicts motion-code sequences from the learned EEG representations, while a final geometric refinement stage improves continuous trajectory reconstruction through motion-level training. Under a last-session test protocol, NeuroMotion achieves the best mean reconstruction performance among the compared EEG decoding baselines across all three datasets, with the clearest gains on full-body motion in both reconstruction accuracy and distribution-level quality. Multi-subject ablations further support the contributions of EEG-to-primitive alignment, token prediction, and refinement. Code is available at https://github.com/Liuyi2351433/NeuroAction.

papers.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI generation. We first train a separate EEG encoder to predict each fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window. After training, we freeze the encoders and project their concatenated hidden features into a shared neurovascular code. Conditioned on this code, stochastic interpolant transforms Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals, allowing different responses to be sampled for the same EEG window. We evaluate our approach on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including four resting-state and four task-based datasets with 61,646 volume-level pairs. Under within-subject and held-out-subject evaluation, our model improves average Pearson correlation over the strongest encoder baselines by 19.1% and 19.8%, respectively. The corresponding improvements over the strongest generator baselines are 18.8% and 47.9%. Beyond reconstruction accuracy, we also evaluate the generated signals using subject-identification classifiers trained on real fMRI. Our method achieves the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated generators. We hope that our work opens up new opportunities for cross-modal brain modeling.

papers.title: Interrater agreement of seizure onset and spread in scalp EEG
papers.abstract: Objective. Faster seizure spread on intracranial EEG has been linked to worse surgical outcome. If contralateral spread on scalp EEG carried similar prognostic information, it could identify poor resection candidates before intracranial monitoring and direct them toward neuromodulation sooner. Testing this first requires that experts reliably annotate spread on scalp EEG. The interrater agreement for seizure spread detection on scalp EEG is unknown; prior scalp EEG reliability studies have focused mainly on seizure detection. We quantified expert agreement on the laterality, channels, and timing of seizure onset and contralateral spread. Methods. We retrospectively analyzed 79 seizures from 48 patients undergoing presurgical evaluation at a single center. Three board certified epileptologists independently marked the time and channels of onset and contralateral spread for each seizure. We measured agreement on onset laterality and spread presence with Gwet k, channels with Cohen k, and timing with the median absolute deviation (MAD). Interrater and majority vote consensus agreement were estimated with patient-clustered CIs. Results. Onset laterality showed substantial interrater agreement (Gwet k = 0.73, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.83); most disagreement involved bilateral onsets. Contralateral spread agreement was comparable (0.63, 0.48 to 0.76). Channel level agreement was higher for onset (inter rater Cohen k = 0.57) than for spread (0.38). Onset timing was highly consistent (median MAD 0.40 s); spread timing agreement was also high (1.99 s), but less so than onset timing (sign rank p < 0.001). Agreement did not differ across annotators or between temporal and non-temporal epilepsy. Significance. Epileptologists generally agree on onset laterality and whether and when seizures spread contralaterally, although spread channels are identified less reliably. These findings support the feasibility of measuring scalp EEG spread as a candidate noninvasive marker of seizure network extent. The public annotated dataset provides a multi-expert reference standard for developing automated spread detection algorithms.

papers.title: Shared Neural Dynamics of Sentence-Level Language Processing in Verbally Proficient Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults
papers.abstract: Autistic individuals often show atypical language development during childhood, yet many attain typical language proficiency by adulthood. This raises the question of whether the neural processes supporting language differ in autism once language has been acquired. Using electroencephalography (EEG), we compared verbally proficient autistic and non-autistic adults during rapid serial visual presentation of structured sentences and pseudoword lists. Sentence processing elicited oscillatory responses across theta, alpha, beta, and gamma frequency bands, with distinct spatiotemporal profiles and hemispheric lateralization most pronounced in the theta, alpha, and beta bands. Notably, beta-band activity increased over sentence position and was positively associated with verbal ability, consistent with a role in the maintenance and integration of linguistic information. These effects were highly comparable across groups, with similar patterns observed at both the individual and group levels and across sensor- and source-level analyses. Together, these findings indicate largely shared neural dynamics of sentence-level language processing in verbally proficient autistic and non-autistic adults, suggesting that atypical language-related neural organization is not an inevitable feature of autism in adulthood.

The results indicate largely shared neural dynamics of sentence-level language processing in both groups.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical applications in diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical decision-making.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy affects approximately 50 million people worldwide, with disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries where access to specialized care remains limited. Despite advances in neuroimaging and electrophysiology, accurate diagnosis, etiological classification, and timely identification of surgical candidates remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to integrate multimodal data and support clinical decision-making across the epilepsy care continuum. To systematically assess and meta-analytically quantify the evidence on AI applications for diagnosis, etiological classification, outcome prediction, surgical candidate selection, and workflow optimization in epilepsy. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251117939). Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, and SciELO for studies published between January 2014 and March 2026. Eligible studies included original research in human subjects with epilepsy applying AI or machine learning models and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric with internal or external validation. Study quality was assessed using PROBAST. Pooled estimates of Area Under the Curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were derived using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models across four clinical task groups: diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical referral. From 423 identified records, 102 studies met inclusion criteria. Research output increased markedly after 2018, peaking in 2021 and 2024, with geographic concentration in China (n = 31) and the United States (n = 11). Electroencephalography and MRI were the dominant input modalities, and Support Vector Machines (n = 41) and Convolutional Neural Networks (n = 22) were the most frequently employed algorithms. Most studies relied exclusively on internal validation, and external validation remained scarce across all domains. PROBAST assessment revealed high risk of bias in the majority of studies, particularly in the participant and analysis domains. Meta-analysis demonstrated strong discriminative performance across all groups: the classification group achieved the highest pooled AUC (0.929; 95% CI: 0.837-0.971), followed by diagnosis (0.899; 95% CI: 0.859-0.929), surgical referral (0.895; 95% CI: 0.870-0.916), and outcome prediction (0.807; 95% CI: 0.740-0.861). Sensitivity was highest in the diagnosis group (0.885; 95% CI: 0.840-0.918) and lowest in surgical referral (0.729; 95% CI: 0.681-0.771), a clinically relevant asymmetry given the high cost of missing true surgical candidates in drug-resistant epilepsy. Substantial variability was observed across studies, reflecting differences in data modalities, AI architectures, and sample sizes, and indicating that pooled estimates should be interpreted with caution rather than as fixed, generalizable performance figures. AI demonstrates robust and clinically meaningful performance across the spectrum of epilepsy care, particularly for diagnosis and surgical planning. However, uniformly high between-study heterogeneity, predominant reliance on internal validation, variable study quality, and underrepresentation of low- and middle-income country contexts limit the generalizability of current evidence and hinder clinical translation. Prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and context-adapted implementation strategies are essential to realize the full clinical potential that this body of evidence consistently demonstrates.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of a psychotherapy-predictive electroencephalographic signature in PTSD.
papers.abstract: Although psychotherapy is at present the most effective treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), its efficacy is still limited for many patients, due mainly to the substantial clinical and neurobiological heterogeneity in the disease. Development of treatment-predictive algorithms by leveraging machine learning on brain connectivity data can advance our understanding of the neurobiological mechanisms underlying the disease and its treatment. Doing so with low-cost and easy-to-gather electroencephalogram (EEG) data may furthermore facilitate clinical translation of such algorithms for patients with PTSD. This study investigates whether individual patient-level resting-state EEG connectivity can predict psychotherapy outcomes in PTSD. We developed a treatment-predictive EEG signature using machine learning applied to high-density resting-state EEG collected from military veterans with PTSD. The predictive signature was dominated by theta frequency EEG connectivity differences and was able to generalize across two types of psychotherapy-prolonged exposure and cognitive processing therapy. Our results also advance a biological definition of a PTSD patient subgroup who is resistant to psychotherapy, which is currently the most evidence-based treatment for the condition. The findings support a path towards clinically translatable and scalable biomarkers that could be used to tailor interventions for each individual or drive the development of novel treatments (ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT03343028).

papers.title: Implementation of nurse-led frontal electroencephalography for early neurological assessment in patients after cardiac arrest: the FRONT study.
papers.abstract: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is a valuable tool for neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest. However, registration is often delayed by time-consuming electrode placement and limited availability of EEG technicians. This study investigated the implementation of a frontal EEG (fEEG) configuration using 6 self-adhesive electrodes by nurses within 3 h of Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission in patients after cardiac arrest. The FRONT study followed a type 3 hybrid design. Nurses were trained to start an fEEG through a theoretical and practical session and were supported by a Step-by-Step interactive guide. Knowledge, attitude, and practice surveys were completed by nurses at baseline and after each fEEG application. Correct and timely application was measured prospectively in 60 patients. At baseline, the survey response rate was 46% (49/107); after application, it was 68% (41/60). Most nurses (84%) reported having sufficient knowledge of fEEG electrode placement and monitoring. The interactive guide was frequently used (98%) during fEEG initiation; the median application time was 20 min [IQR: 15-25]. All nurses found early fEEG monitoring meaningful; perception improved since implementation (3.98 ± 0.78 vs 4.54 ± 0.51, p < 0.001). During the implementation, an fEEG was applied in 88% of patients (53/60), including 73% (44/60) within 3 h. Electrode placement was confirmed as correct by EEG technicians in all evaluated patients. ICU nurses were able to apply fEEG monitoring with high levels of adoption, acceptability and fidelity following a short, multifaceted training program combined with an interactive guide. Further research is needed to clarify the interpretability, diagnostic performance, prognostic value, and clinical utility of nurse-led fEEG monitoring in post-resuscitation care. Early bedside EEG assessment by trained ICU nurses may facilitate timely neurological evaluation in routine clinical practice.

papers.title: Fluorescence spectroscopy coupled with dual-modal cross-attention feature fusion for accurate quantification of microplastics in agricultural soils.
papers.abstract: Microplastic contamination in agricultural soils has emerged as a critical environmental issue, posing potential risks to soil ecosystems, food security, and human health. However, rapid and accurate quantification of soil microplastics remains challenging due to the limited sensitivity and feature extraction capability of conventional spectroscopic methods. To address these limitations, this study develops a fluorescence spectroscopy-based dual-modal cross-attention feature fusion (DM-CAFF) framework for the intelligent quantification of microplastics in agricultural soils. A total of 2400 fluorescence emission spectra were collected from soil samples containing different microplastic types, particle sizes, concentration levels, and soil backgrounds. First, to enhance spectral information representation, one-dimensional fluorescence spectra were transformed into improved two-dimensional gramian angular field (GAF) images, enabling the simultaneous characterization of local spectral variations and global distribution patterns. After that, variational autoencoder (VAE) and conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE)-based augmentation strategies were employed to expand the dataset and improve sample diversity. Finally, a dual-modal learning framework was subsequently constructed to jointly exploit spectral sequence information and image-based spatial features. The proposed DM-CAFF framework achieved superior performance compared with conventional spectral analysis methods and existing fusion models, yielding a coefficient of determination for prediction (R2p) of 0.9757, root mean square error of prediction (RMSEp) of 0.4437 wt%, mean absolute error of prediction (MAEp) of 0.1173 wt%, and residual predictive deviation (RPDp) of 6.4147. In addition, excellent classification performance was obtained for seven categories of soil microplastics. The developed DM-CAFF framework provides a reliable technical reference for rapid quantitative detection of microplastics in agricultural soils.

papers.title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology.
papers.abstract: Imperceptible skin electronic interfaces for bidirectional communication are essential for next‑generation healthcare and human-machine interfaces. The long‑standing absence of an ideal interfacing material has made it challenging to achieve high‑quality bidirectional electrophysiology without disturbing innate perception. Inspired by the human stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, we report a metallic stratum corneum (MSC): a synthetic mesohydrous gel reinforced with a silver nanowire network. MSC achieves > 106 S m-1 conductivity, dual‑mode (electronic/ionic) conduction, sub-micron thickness, and months‑long ambient stability. Its porous ultrathin architecture enables multidimensional imperceptibility (tactile, mechanical, thermal, and vapor‑permeable). MSC records electrophysiology with signal‑to‑noise ratio surpassing commercial gel electrodes, delivers efficient neuromuscular stimulation, and forms high‑resolution electrode arrays for spatiotemporal muscle mapping. By reconciling electronic performance, skin compatibility, and imperceptibility, the mesohydrous gel establishes a promising material platform for next-generation on-skin bioelectronics.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.abstract: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardized resource of hierarchically organized phenotypic terms used for deep phenotyping, both in research and diagnosis. In our study, we aimed to investigate how the specificity of EEG-related HPO terms may impact phenotype and gene scoring and prioritization. We compiled three HPO-based profiles, differing only in EEG terms: (a) a full profile, including all EEG-specific terms; (b) a profile containing only the non-specific EEG term ("HP:0002353" EEG abnormality); and (c) a profile without any EEG terms. We identified a total of 185 HPO terms across 33 pediatric patients with epilepsy, with a median of 2 EEG-related terms per patient. Analysis included both phenotypic and gene scoring for each profile. We observed significantly higher scores for the non-specific and no-EEG profiles in both the phenotype and combined Exomiser scores. This effect was also observed in patients whose top gene did not change. The full profile returned the shortest candidate lists, with a median of 82 genes, followed by the no-EEG profile (142 genes) and non-specific EEG (157 genes). The top-ranked gene changed in 24-55% of patients across profile comparisons, while the full-profile top gene remained within the top three in 30/33 (non-specific EEG) and 26/33 (no-EEG) patients. Our study shows that more specific EEG-related HPO terms were associated with lower phenotype and combined Exomiser scores and changed the top-ranked gene in a subset of patients. These findings suggest that EEG-related HPO terms should be curated carefully in phenotype-driven variant prioritization. HPO terms are widely used in both clinical and research settings to provide a standardized phenotype description. In this study, we examined how EEG-related HPO terms impact variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy. We found that profiles with specific EEG terms were associated with lower phenotype and gene scores compared with those without EEG terms or with non-specific EEG abnormalities. These findings suggest that the choice of EEG-related HPO terms can influence phenotype-driven prioritization results.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted fusion of urinary Raman and fluorescence spectra for detection of urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Urothelial carcinoma (UC) diagnosis still relies on invasive procedures such as cystoscopy, motivating the development of non-invasive urine-based alternatives. Here, we investigate a multimodal spectroscopic approach combining Raman with UV-excited and VIS-excited fluorescence measurements for UC detection from unprocessed urine using fibre-optic probes. A cohort of 285 patients was analyzed, including 120 UC cases and 165 controls. Spectral analysis revealed consistent biochemical differences between groups, associated with variations in key urinary constituents such as NADH, flavins, porphyrins, urea, and amino acids, supporting the diagnostic potential of urine composition. Two machine learning strategies were evaluated. A PCA-LDA classifier integrating multimodal features achieved moderately low performance (∼64% accuracy), highlighting both the feasibility of spectral data fusion and the limitations of linear methods for complex datasets. In contrast, an artificial neural network (ANN) applied to full spectral data significantly improved classification performance, reaching accuracies above 90% when combined with data augmentation. These results demonstrate that the multimodal spectroscopy approach, particularly when coupled with advanced machine learning strategies, can enable effective non-invasive detection of UC. Despite limitations related to fibre-probe measurements and bulk urine variability, the proposed approach represents a promising step toward rapid and cost-effective bladder cancer screening.

papers.title: Beyond Patching: Consistent Circuit Discovery via Gradient Spectral Analysis
papers.abstract: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to reverse-engineer neural networks by identifying small, faithful subgraphs--circuits--that implement specific behaviors. The dominant paradigm scores each unit by replacing its clean activation with a corrupted counterpart as causal intervention. While effective, this approach rests on a brittle prerequisite: the structure prompt pairs are task-specific, expensive to engineer, and silently couple the discovered circuit to prompt-design choices. In this work, we propose Spectral Circuit Analysis (SCA), a gradient-spectral pipeline that achieves consistent circuit discovery along both axes: stable across input formulations of the same task, and natively exposing structure shared across tasks. Our contributions are threefold. First, we provide a counterfactual-free reframing of circuit discovery: causally relevant directions are recoverable from the spectral structure of forward gradients across paraphrases, with leading directions concentrating task signal and trailing ones absorbing paraphrase noise, yielding circuits tied to the task rather than the prompt. Second, we introduce SCA, a block-wise SVD pipeline that extracts a task subspace per architectural block and redistributes spectral energy onto constituent units via a consistency-weighted share, producing per-unit rankings competitive with attribution-patching baselines under strictly less supervision. Finally, on twelve circuit-discovery tasks in GPT-2 Small and Pythia-160M, SCA performs comparably or exceeds EAP-family methods under the standard recovery-score protocol and recovers IOI canonical heads with Precision@K = 1.0 in top-10 slices on GPT-2 Small; the same machinery extends to a unified cross-task analysis classifying units as universal, family-shared, or task-specific and exposing compositional structure invisible to per-task analyses.
